description.en: A travelling archivist discovers the city's maps rearrange themselves overnight, and only the oldest residents remember why.
After the lantern festival ends, two rival apprentices realise the river has stopped reflecting their faces.
A disgraced courier takes one last job across a country where the roads vanish behind her.
In a port where the tides keep letters from reaching their senders, a boy builds a boat out of unanswered mail.
The last repairer of a dying craft gets a visitor who claims to be the first.
A quiet winter town starts receiving packages addressed to people who were never born.
An orphan inherits a greenhouse whose plants only bloom when someone tells them the truth.
A detective investigates a series of thefts in which only the frames of paintings are stolen.
The two moons disagree on when night should end, and a shepherd is caught between their arguments.
A sailor returns home to find her village has moved three valleys to the west.
On the morning of her coronation, a princess is handed a letter written in her own future handwriting.
A cartographer draws a city that doesn't exist yet, and the city starts correcting her mistakes.
The library of a mountain monastery files new books every full moon; nobody writes them.
A clockmaker is paid in minutes borrowed from a stranger's life, and keeps very careful ledgers.
An apprentice baker learns that the oldest recipes in the house were written by her, in a hand she doesn't remember.
Two musicians who have never met start composing opposite halves of the same unfinished song.
A lamplighter in a town without night is told the sun has been reading her mind.
A gardener who speaks only to bees is nominated to settle a border dispute between two kingdoms.
An elderly dancer agrees to teach a reluctant student one last routine; neither of them knows the music yet.
A rural post office handles mail from a country that no longer appears on any map, and the postmistress refuses to retire.
A traveller carries a mirror that remembers everyone it has ever reflected, and loses it at a crowded festival.
The village's youngest blacksmith is apprenticed to a stranger whose hammer makes no sound.
A shut-in novelist starts receiving corrected drafts of her next book, in her own handwriting, by courier.
A pair of twins born on either side of a border grow up as rivals and inherit the same inconvenient gift.
A town built on an old lighthouse learns that the beam has been pointing at the wrong things on purpose.
A retired explorer agrees to lead one more expedition, provided the destination is a place she has already been.
A woman wakes up with other people's memories of her, and sets out to find out who she was in them.
A quiet neighbourhood bookshop keeps selling the same single-print volume to the same regular, who never reads it.
A journeyman carpenter is hired to rebuild a theatre that was never built in the first place.
A reluctant diplomat is sent to a kingdom whose language she doesn't share with anyone else who speaks it.
